children: Enveda, a privately held AI biotechnology startup, has doubled its valuation to about $2 billion as momentum builds behind tech-driven approaches to discovering new medicines.

The financing will help the Boulder, Colo.-based company fund later-stage human trials. Healthcare investor Catalio Capital Management led the latest financing round alongside technology funds such as Iconiq, which includes backing from former Johnson & Johnson Chief Executive Alex Gorsky.
Enveda is part of a growing wave of biotech startups using artificial intelligence to streamline early stage drug discovery, a process historically marked by high costs and long timelines.
Using its AI platform Prism, Enveda identifies and ranks therapeutic compounds found in plants and microbes, predicting their structures and biological functions to generate new treatments.

Enveda's platform has produced 17 drug candidates since 2019, and the company says it can identify commercially viable molecules roughly four times faster and at one-tenth the cost of traditional methods.

"The industry has gotten really, really good at commercializing a molecule once you know it's right, but has increasingly gotten worse at finding the right molecule," Enveda Chief Executive Viswa Colluru said. "We're letting AI lead the way for answers that already exist in nature."

The company has an experimental daily pill designed to help patients maintain weight loss after discontinuing GLP-1 medications. It is expected to soon begin mid-stage testing. Enveda said it found the drug by decoding the chemistry released by the body during intense physical activity, identifying a hormone that naturally suppresses appetite.
Enveda is also advancing a pill for atopic dermatitis that cleared patients' skin in an early stage clinical trial. A third drug, for inflammatory bowel disease, is currently in Phase 1 testing.
Enveda has expanded its leadership team over the past year, hiring Novo Nordisk's former head of disease prevention.
